Four campaigns, one studio

Four niches, four briefs, one renderer. A campaign is now a JSON file and a folder of pictures — the studio lists them, the admin form writes them, and the engine reads the same file with no second copy to keep in sync.

Same campaign, mascot style

When an agency supplies a mascot, nothing about the campaign changes — same spec, same ranked array, same required mention. Only the renderer differs.

The interface

Runs locally on the Next app. Verified end to end this session: a campaign was created through the form, listed in the studio, and rendered — five slides in 5.5 seconds.

Studio

/studio

Pick a campaign and a style. The panel above the button shows what the brief locks — rate, budget left, review window, aspect, required mention, banned claims — so a clipper sees the terms before rendering, not after rejection. Mascot style is disabled with a reason when the campaign has no mascot asset.

Admin

/admin/new

Agency onboarding: brand, terms, banned claims, palette, photo folder, optional mascot, then the hook, the ranked payload and the closer. Saves the exact JSON the engine reads.

Render API

POST /api/sets

Renders and returns slide URLs with the logic-check verdict. A copy line that will not fit comes back as a 422 naming the line, because "render failed" tells an operator nothing they can act on.

File API

GET /api/file/…

Serves rendered slides. The path is resolved and then checked against output/, so a traversal cannot escape — verified: 403 on a campaign JSON, 404 on ../.env.local.

Verified, not asserted

POST /api/specs   {"id":"core-creatine",…}     -> saved: core-creatine
POST /api/sets    {"campaignId":"core-creatine"} -> 5 slides in 5.5s · logic PASS
GET  /api/file/output/sets/…/slide-1.png        -> 200 image/png 1,182,296b
GET  /api/file/campaigns/apex-strength.json     -> 403 forbidden
GET  /api/file/../.env.local                    -> 404 not found
GET  /api/specs                                 -> apex-strength, core-creatine, fuel-prep, ledger-money

What the renderer learned this round

  • Captions on facesThe band solver measured how busy a region was, which cannot see a face — a face in flat light is one of the quietest things in a frame, which is exactly how the money set put its hook across a man's eyes. Bands now carry a skin-tone share, weighted heavily.
  • Quiet band, loud blockWorse: the block was anchored at a band's top and allowed to grow past it, so a quiet strip only guaranteed its own 158px. The caption is now fitted first to learn its real height, then windows of that height are scored and ranked.
  • Zone cut off the best spotThe hook's search zone started at 10% of frame height, which excluded the band above the subject's head — the single best placement in a portrait. It starts at 5% now.
